suggestions.assertion: Headings tell the story: at least half of the body headings state a claim, finding or question rather than a generic topic label like 'Overview', 'Status' or 'Details'
suggestions.reason: The verdict hinges on an undefined denominator and on whether item-name headings count. Over all headings this output scores about 26%; over the human zone only, 43%; it reaches half only if the six 'Qn <topic>' headings are counted as question headings. Lettered reference blocks (A-H) legitimately carry label headings. Specify the scope (human zone only?) and a test for a qualifying heading (for example contains a verb, a number or an outcome, or ends with '?').

suggestions.assertion: Glance first: the first section after the title is a one-screen overview ...
suggestions.reason: 'One screen' and 'first 60 source lines' diverge: the glance section is 43 source lines but renders to about two screens because of the embedded picture, the six-item ask list and the risk table, and the check passes on line count. Consider a stricter operational test, such as verdict plus asks inside the first ~30 lines, or a cap on the number of elements.

suggestions.assertion: Dana's view: the first screen says where things stand (how many of the 11 tasks are done, blocked or open) ...
suggestions.reason: This passes with '3 of 11 tasks done, 4 blockers' and no open count, and two of the five decisions (email, cron owner) carry an imperative ask but no labelled option or recommendation. Require all three counts and a recommendation per decision, or relax the wording so a pass means the same thing for every output.

suggestions.assertion: Evidence out of the way ... / No leakage ...
suggestions.reason: These two overlap heavily (both ask that raw material and dead ends stay out of Dana's part) and are satisfied by the same facts. Consider merging them and adding a size budget for the human zone (here 192 of 390 lines, about half the document) or a jargon/path-density check: Dana's part contains 23 inline code identifiers and a technical 'How the new setup works' paragraph yet passes.

Both pass on the same heading ('START HERE - at a glance'). Neither requires the banner to say who the part is for, although the first says 'name the audience'; the person glyph and 'START HERE' were accepted. Merge them, or require the word for Dana/people in the banner.

No assertion checks fidelity to the notes or honest labelling of assumptions. This output added content the notes do not contain (an 'Allowed without asking' permission model, time-boxes, an untested xlsxwriter hint, CET/CEST conversion, recommendations for Q2-Q4 and Q6) and labelled it as assumption or inference in section 5 and block E. A discriminating assertion would spot-check key figures (3 of 11 done; 9.5/21/15 min; 1,200 USD/month; 11 of 14 cron jobs; DBA window Tue/Thu 22:00-23:00 UTC; back on a Saturday) and require invented or inferred items to be labelled.

'Continue without asking me anything' is the core requirement for the agent part, but no assertion checks the protocol for pending decisions. The output has an Answer column, a 'stop, do not invent work' rule, a stale-status update rule and a progress log; an assertion such as 'the agent part says what to do while Q1-Q4 are open and where answers are recorded' would reward this and punish handoffs that only list tasks.

eval_feedback.overall: Most assertions test for structural features that this output satisfies, so they discriminate weakly; the single fail comes from an ambiguous heading metric. The assertions do not check factual fidelity, labelling of assumptions, or how the agent handles unanswered decisions, which matter most in a handoff.
